title: Nursing student who resells thrifted clothes promised 'no takeout this week'; two fast-food charges sit in her bank by Sunday night, but a charge can't break a promise, so Dev asks and only her answer decides

changes.content: I'm not getting any takeout this week, only cooking at home

dev_must_notice.what: On Mon Nov 9 at 8:05 PM she told Dev she wouldn't get any takeout this week. It is Sunday Nov 15, 9 PM, the check-in time. Her bank shows a Chipotle charge of $14.60 on Wed Nov 11 and a pending McDonald's charge of $17.69 on Sat Nov 14, so it looks like a broken promise, but a charge doesn't say who ate it or why: it could be for a roommate she was paying back, a gift, a group order, or a charge she is counting as not hers. Nothing in her data is her answer, and no to-do is linked to this promise. Dev asks once and waits for her answer.

best_fix.what: One check-in at 9 PM, after her Sunday call home, in plain words: "You said no takeout this week. How did it go?" with three answers: [Yes, I did it] [Tomorrow instead] [It didn't happen]. The message never mentions the Chipotle or McDonald's charges. Yes is recorded as kept, warmly. Tomorrow instead moves the check to 9 PM Monday (at most twice). It didn't happen is recorded as broken, honestly and gently, and offers a smaller promise for next week (for example, two takeout-free dinners). If she doesn't answer, nothing is recorded; after 7 days the promise is dropped and never counted as broken.
best_fix.why: The promise is hers. Only her own answer settles it, and a bank charge is not her answer: what looks like takeout in the data may not be what she meant. Asking without citing the charges keeps the check-in kind and accurate, and avoids a message that reads like being watched.

must_not: mark the promise broken because of the Chipotle or McDonald's charges (a charge is never her answer)
mark it kept because the grocery run, her Sunday call or the week's quiet days exist, or because she didn't reply
quote the Chipotle or McDonald's charges in the check-in or say "I saw you ordered..."
use guilt words ("you slipped", "you broke it", "you failed") or ask why she ordered
send the check-in before 9 PM Sunday or ask again tonight if she doesn't reply
count the open payouts or any future eBay or Poshmark sale as money she has, or predict next week's payout
comment on her spending in other categories (thrift sourcing, shipping and coffee are part of her resale business and routines)
send the check-in during her Sunday 8:00 to 8:45 PM call home
assumptions: 'No takeout this week' is a promise (keeping her word is the point) and not a to-do or goal; Dev saved it when she said it, with check-in time Sunday 9 PM.
The pending McDonald's charge posts Monday; pending charges are shown but are not a reason to decide anything.
The Poshmark payout line shows the same 'EBAY COMM PAYOUT' text as eBay's in the simulator; both are marketplace payouts of $40.60 and $49.42 on Nov 9.
Her Sunday call home is 8 to 8:45 PM; 9 PM follows it.
Marketplace payouts vary week to week; Dev never predicts them. December rent share is $775.10 on Dec 1 and checking holds $980.00 available, so money is not the issue in this case.

tempting.suggestion: send the check-in during her Sunday 8:00 to 8:45 PM call home
tempting.why_wrong: Sunday evening call home is a firm routine; the check-in waits until 9 PM, after it
